findings.summary: Delegation bullets mix two ideas, and the page's own remember note conflicts slightly with the bullets: "closest() then contains()" is stated as a rule but the first delegation bullet says only to inspect event.target.
findings.evidence: "One listener on a parent; inspect event.target, no binding per child" vs "Never trust e.target alone: always closest() then contains()."
findings.fix: Split the first bullet into "One listener on the parent" and "No binding per child", and say "resolve the item with e.target.closest()" instead of "inspect event.target".

findings.summary: Passive-listener section is a dense bullet run mixing defaults, exceptions and behavior, with two near-duplicate code blocks that could be one comparison table.
findings.evidence: "Default applies only on window, document, body" / "On other elements, wheel is non-passive unless passive: true" / "preventDefault() in a passive listener is ignored and warns in the console"
findings.fix: Replace the bullets and two code blocks with a small table (passive true/false vs preventDefault effect) and one line on which events are passive by default.

findings.summary: Page 4 states the passive-by-default rule inconsistently: touchstart, touchmove and wheel are passive by default, then only on window/document/body, which a skimmer will misread.
findings.evidence: "touchstart, touchmove, wheel are passive by default" followed by "Default applies only on window, document, body"
findings.fix: Merge into one bullet: "touchstart, touchmove, wheel are passive by default only on window, document, body."

findings.summary: The Reading and validating section crams several ideas (FormData, single fields, validity API, search-box advice, debounce) into one run of bullets; code appears before the idea is stated.
findings.evidence: javascript form.addEventListener('submit', e => { ... }) appears directly under the heading before any one-line idea
findings.fix: State the idea first ("preventDefault, validate, then read via FormData"), and move the search-box/debounce bullets into their own labelled group or the Mistakes section.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet says passive matters only for touchstart, touchmove and wheel, which is too narrow.
findings.evidence: passive matters only for touchstart, touchmove, wheel
findings.fix: Say that passive mainly matters for scroll-blocking events such as touchstart, touchmove and wheel (and the legacy mousewheel). Say that passive: true makes preventDefault a no-op on any event type.

findings.summary: Cheat sheet bullet packs two ideas (passive scope and the removal rule) in loose lines, and the mixed-options code example adds little.
findings.evidence: "Remove with the same fn reference or ac.abort(); inline arrows can't be removed"
findings.fix: Split into separate one-idea bullets: "Remove: same fn reference" and "Remove: ac.abort() via signal".
